title: Magnetic field magnitude
description: Essential: The final answer for part (1) must be correctly calculated as B = E cosθ / v₀, yielding √3 T or approximately 1.73 T.

title: Electric field time
description: Essential: The final answer for part (2) must include the correct time in the electric field, t₁ = (m v₀ tanθ)/(qE) or equivalent, yielding approximately 1.67e-05 s.

title: Magnetic field time
description: Essential: The final answer for part (2) must include the correct time in the magnetic field, t₂ = (m θ)/(qB) or equivalent, with θ in radians, yielding approximately 1.74e-05 s.

title: Electric field kinematics
description: Important: The solution must correctly relate the vertical velocity gain (v_y = v₀ tanθ) to the electric force acceleration (v_y = (qE/m) t₁) to find t₁ or the width d.

title: Magnetic force geometry
description: Important: The solution must apply the Lorentz force as centripetal force (qv₀B = mv₀²/r) and use the geometry of the circular arc (r = d/sinθ) to relate B to given parameters.

title: Arc time calculation
description: Important: For the magnetic field time, the solution must correctly calculate the arc length (s = rθ) and divide by the constant speed v₀, using the angle in radians.

title: Unit consistency
description: Optional: The solution should demonstrate consistent use of SI units (V/m, m/s, rad) and correctly handle the charge-to-mass ratio.

title: Sign or angle error
description: Pitfall: Deduct if the student uses the deflection angle incorrectly (e.g., uses sinθ instead of cosθ in B formula, or uses degrees instead of radians for arc length).

title: Force confusion
description: Pitfall: Deduct if the student confuses electric and magnetic force kinematics (e.g., applies parabolic motion in the magnetic field or uniform circular motion in the electric field).
